name: Day One, Day Ninety
why_it_works: People do not believe a promise, but they believe a timeline. Showing the plain starting point, the boring middle and then the result makes change feel reachable, and hiding day ninety until last keeps people watching to see if it worked.

hook.pattern: Show day one, cover day ninety with a blur or card, and promise the honest middle.
examples: Day one vs day ninety. No filters, no tricks.
Day one is real. Day ninety is last.
Ninety days with {{brand}}. This is what changed.

craft.notes: Lock the day-one and day-ninety photos to the same spot, height, lens and light so the only variable is the person. Name the habits in plain words in the middle; the process is what makes the result believable.

do_not: Generate or AI-edit a client's before or after photo; use real, consented photos for those frames and only generate backgrounds or title cards
Change lighting, pose or clothing between before and after to exaggerate the result
Pick only your single best client and imply it is typical
compliance: Med spa and dental: written patient consent for every before/after image; add 'Results vary. Individual results not guaranteed.' on screen
Med spa and dental: name the actual treatment, number of sessions and provider type; no retouching of before/after photos
Chiropractor: no claims of curing conditions; describe what the patient reported, not a medical promise
Fitness and coaching: no guaranteed weight, income or timeline outcomes; state that results vary
Before/after frames use real, consented client photos only (real_photo); never generate or AI-edit the client
